sources.title: W3C MediaStream Recording
sources.observed_operation: Read current published W3C HTML specification
sources.condition_default_exception: Omitted MIME hint permits UA default; supplied MIME constrains format; start/track/error paths can fail asynchronously; timeslice can be longer than requested; individual blobs need not be playable, completed concatenation must be.
sources.applicability: Governing lifecycle, MIME, pause/resume, chunk assembly, bounds; working-draft recommendations require browser feature detection.

sources.title: W3C Media Capture and Streams
sources.version_or_commit: Current published URL, accessed 2026-10-10; no pinned version in URL
sources.locator: Sections 4.3.1, 5.2, 8, 9, 14; actual getSettings around lines 636-649; sampleRate constraints lines 790-860 and ideal/exact semantics 1993-1995, 2252-2268; examples 2093-2113
sources.observed_operation: Read permission, track lifecycle, device enumeration, and sampleRate constraint/settings sections
sources.condition_default_exception: Permission/device errors reject getUserMedia; mute is temporary; ended covers revocation/device removal; devicechange reports changed device set; sampleRate can be exact/ideal and actual settings are read from getSettings(); stop() is own cleanup and does not fire ended.
sources.applicability: Microphone-only permission/start behavior, mute/ended/input changes, cleanup.

sources.title: W3C Web Audio API 1.1
sources.version_or_commit: Web Audio API 1.1 current published specification
sources.locator: Section 1.32 AudioWorklet; AudioWorkletGlobalScope/Processor; sections 2.5-2.6 render quantum; process algorithm
sources.observed_operation: Read specification definitions and processing algorithm
sources.condition_default_exception: AudioWorklet code runs on rendering thread; port messages bridge contexts; default render quantum 128 frames but can be configured; processor errors and ports have lifecycle semantics.
sources.applicability: Custom PCM capture mechanism; worklet does not define a recording encoder/container.

sources.title: WebKit Features in Safari 14.1
sources.locator: MediaRecorder API and WebM Support, lines 69-78
sources.condition_default_exception: WebKit added MediaStream Recording with platform defaults; adjacent WebM statement refers to playback on macOS, not WebM recording.
sources.applicability: Safari release history only, not a current capability denial.

sources.title: WebKit Features in Safari 18.4
sources.condition_default_exception: MediaRecorder WebM with Opus and VP8/VP9, fragmented MP4, ALAC/PCM; Ogg Opus/Vorbis explicitly for macOS Sequoia 15.4, iOS/iPadOS 18.4, visionOS 2.4.
sources.applicability: Runtime candidate formats on matching Safari/OS releases; MIME exactness and capture still require probes.

sources.title: WebKit Features in Safari 26.0
sources.locator: Media section; `audio/mp4; codecs=alac` example and WebCodecs addition
sources.condition_default_exception: Release says ALAC/PCM in MediaRecorder and adds AudioEncoder/AudioDecoder; explicit ALAC MIME example.
sources.applicability: Version-bounded Safari candidate, not success in other releases/platforms.

sources.title: Apple Safari 17.4 Release Notes
sources.observed_operation: Read official Apple search-result excerpts for version/date and Media > Resolved Issues; direct page body was not exposed
sources.condition_default_exception: Release item says pausing MediaRecorder continued `ondataavailable` at every timeslice; fixed in this release.
sources.applicability: Pause/timeslice regression history for exact Safari 17.4 release.

sources.title: WebKit Bug 258567: empty MediaRecorder Blobs
sources.observed_operation: Read WebKit bug report and discussion
sources.condition_default_exception: M1/Ventura 13.4.1 reporter saw empty audio/mp4 at 96 kHz system output; their reload after switching output to 48 kHz worked; maintainer did not reproduce.
sources.applicability: Incident test motivation only; not a general browser claim.

sources.title: WebKit Bug 243837: extra bytes after pause/requestData/stop
sources.observed_operation: Read public issue and linked commit record
sources.condition_default_exception: Specific sequence start, pause, requestData, stop; reported additional bytes/truncation; fix committed.
sources.applicability: Historic Safari finalization sequence; original example was iOS, not current desktop mic.

sources.title: Chrome Developers: Record audio and video with MediaRecorder
sources.locator: Support notes and MIME examples, lines 50-73 onward
sources.observed_operation: Read official Google Chrome Developers article
sources.condition_default_exception: Audio support Chrome 49+, Chrome 47/48 video-only behind flag; shows audio/webm and omitted options default.
sources.applicability: Historical release detail only; not a current support table.

sources.title: Chromium muxer README
sources.version_or_commit: Exact Chromium commit 042aaa189184e3d303c01946589eb84926d91000; not branded Chrome release
sources.condition_default_exception: Muxers primarily used by MediaRecorder; WebM Opus and MP4 Opus/AAC listed.
sources.applicability: Candidate architecture/types only; no public runtime support guarantee.

sources.title: opus-media-recorder npm package
sources.version_or_commit: Registry displayed package 0.8.0, MIT, last published about five years before access
sources.locator: README architecture/how-to/use/limitations and npm package version fields
sources.observed_operation: Read npm page and package README; no install/run
sources.condition_default_exception: WebAssembly encoders plus Web Worker and static asset/bundler setup; Ogg/WebM/WAV. README says WAV slices are complete independent files and cannot be concatenated; generic errors/no video.
sources.applicability: Established alternative analogy and cost/risk, not current browser support evidence.

research_limitations: No Chrome or Safari browser/version was specified or executed.
No browser runtime permission, capability, constructor, capture, playback, or download observation was made.
Vendor codec announcements do not establish exact audio-only MIME-string behavior on an unpinned runtime.
